about: What a landscape gardener may change in the Verge design. Protected: the scroll-run makeover of a back garden from above (surveyed, cleared, built, turfed, planted, grown in at dusk; job.style picks sandstone and flowering borders or porcelain and grasses), the rough-price builder, the care calendar, the booking, layout, type and all interaction code. The gardener's own words, job numbers, units, features and prices, months, plans and visit steps come from the content.
rules: Text may not contain < > { } or line breaks.

job: the example makeover the hero runs. style picks the look of the build: cottage (sandstone patio, curved lawn, flowering borders) or modern (porcelain, straight lines, grasses). area, tonnes cleared, plants and days on site are shown in the tally; dims are the garden's width and length for the survey tapes, in units.length.
units: area (m², sq ft) and length (m, ft), used in the hero, the size slider and the price.
stages: six steps, in order: survey, clear, build, turf, plant, grown in. Each a short name, a caption and when it happens (Week 1, Next June).

quote.features: two to eight things a customer can ask for, each with an icon (patio, lawn, planting, path, lighting, fencing, decking, water), a fixed part (from), a part per unit of area (rate), days on site (days, plus per100 for every 100 units of area). The first two start picked. quote.finish: the standard finish (x 1) first. quote.size: the slider's range and starting size, in units.area, with a hint. quote.spread: the range either side of the middle estimate.
care.months: January to December, each with its season, a short line, the visits that month and one to four jobs. care.plans: up to three care plans with a price per visit.
book: visit times, more answers for what you'd like (after the features), days closed (0 Sunday to 6 Saturday), up to four steps of how it goes, and the postcode or ZIP label with an example.
